item.title: Generating Random Uuids On Oracle A Quick Guide

Here’s an example of how to do that: -- Generate random number (between 0 and 2^32-1) WITH random_num AS ( SELECT DBMS_RANDOM.VALUE(0, POWER(2, 32) - 1) AS num FROM dual ) -- Convert random number to UUID format SELECT TO_CHAR(UPPER(HEXTORAW(RPAD(RPAD(LTRIM(TO_CHAR(num, 'XXXXXX')), 8, '0'), 32, '0'))), 'XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX') AS random_uuid FROM random_num; This approach converts a randomly generated number into a UUID format following the guidelines in RFC 4122 .

item.title: Google Bigquery Limit Array Elements In Bigquery Table Get First N
item.description: How to get the first N elements from an array column in a BigQuery table without unnesting, ranking, and aggregating back to an array? Solution A general solution with a User-Defined Function (UDF) that can be called for any array type is as follows: CREATE TEMP FUNCTION TopN(arr ANY TYPE, n INT64) AS ( ARRAY(SELECT x FROM UNNEST(arr) AS x WITH OFFSET off WHERE off < n ORDER BY off) ); WITH data AS ( SELECT 1001 as id, ['a', 'b', 'c'] as array_1 UNION ALL SELECT 1002 as id, ['d', 'e', 'f', 'g'] as array_1 UNION ALL SELECT 1003 as id, ['h', 'i'] as array_1 ) SELECT *, TopN(array_1, 2) AS my_result FROM data The above code first defines a UDF called TopN that takes two inputs - an array and a number, and returns the first N elements of the array while keeping the array data type.

item.description: Question: How can I round a timestamp to the nearest 15-minute interval using BigQuery standard SQL? Solution: To round a timestamp to the nearest 15-minute interval in BigQuery standard SQL, you can use the following formula: TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(900 * DIV(UNIX_SECONDS(dt_from) + 450, 900)) This formula works by converting the timestamp to Unix time (the number of seconds since January 1, 1970), adding 450 seconds (7.5 minutes) to it, dividing the result by 900 (the number of seconds in 15 minutes), rounding down to the nearest integer, and then multiplying by 900 to get the Unix time of the nearest 15-minute interval.

Although, I can provide you with a general idea of SQL anti-patterns. SQL anti-patterns are practices that do more harm than good in SQL programming. Some of the most common SQL anti-patterns include: Using SELECT * instead of specifying required columns in the query Using nested queries or subqueries without proper indexing Using correlated subqueries or cursors instead of set-based logic Using scalar or aggregate functions unnecessarily in SELECT or WHERE clauses Using string concatenation instead of parameterized queries for dynamic SQL Using inconsistent data types for columns or parameters Using hard-coded values instead of using variables or parameters Not using primary keys, foreign keys, or unique constraints in tables Not normalizing tables or using denormalized data Using triggers or stored procedures when not necessary or misusing them To avoid SQL anti-patterns, it is recommended to follow best practices and guidelines for SQL programming, use standard SQL syntax, normalize tables properly, and optimize queries for performance.

item.title: How to connect SSIS to Azure SQL Database?
item.description: Connecting to an Azure SQL database from SSIS is a great way to transfer data from on-premise systems to the cloud. Azure SQL databases offer a secure, scalable, and cost-effective database solution for your data needs. This article will provide a detailed overview on how to connect SSIS to an Azure SQL database, as well as some potential challenges you may encounter along the way. Introduction of Azure SQL Database Azure SQL Database is a cloud-based database service that provides organizations with a fully managed and reliable relational database platform.

item.title: Top 10 Best Practices for Azure SQL Databases
item.description: Azure SQL Databases are cloud-based database services offered by Microsoft Azure. It is a fully managed relational database service that is based on the Microsoft SQL Server database engine. It provides an enterprise-level database solution that is highly available, secure, and scalable. It is designed to meet the needs of companies of all sizes, from small businesses to large enterprises. With Azure SQL Database, organizations can easily deploy, manage, and scale their database workloads with the assurance of enterprise-grade security and reliability.
